messages:
Maya (CS): Heads-up — Velvet Thera is asking for a temporary UK peering + rate limit relaxation for a partner demo tomorrow morning. They reported 300–600ms tail latency from UK users and are worried about the renewal pilot.
Ravi (CS): Customer reported spike from 10k -> 60k requests/hr during internal load test. They want a short QPS bump and an allowlist for a couple proxy IPs.
Maya (CS): Summary of asks from Velvet: 1) Allowlist three CIDRs for their partner edge (listed below). 2) Increase request QPS from 200 -> 800 for 48 hours starting 2024-11-08T08:00Z. 3) Route UK region traffic to eu-west-2 peering if possible. They want auto-rollback after window.
Lina (NetOps): Can you paste the CIDRs and a sample header so we can validate? We'll need signed approval from their security contact per policy.
Ravi (CS): CIDRs and sample header (from customer): ```
# Allowed sources
34.210.128.0/22
34.211.0.0/16
3.8.12.0/24
# Forwarded header
X-VT-Orig-Proxy: 52.17.34.12
```
Maya (CS): They provided signed approval in the ticket — attached in the support portal. I'll post link in a sec.
velvet-bot: Ticket VT-4821 created by velvet-support. SLA: standard. Attachments: approval.pdf
Tom (Infra): Quick notes — planned change: 1) create temporary allowlist rule in perimeter ACL chain with expiry metadata. 2) adjust rate window: global customer QPS cap from 200 to 800, per-route cap unchanged. 3) add route priority to favor eu-west-2 peering for UK/GB ASN ranges. I can do the ACL + rate change if NetOps ok with peering tweak.
Lina (NetOps): Peering tweak looks fine but need to schedule during low risk window and monitor BGP churn. I'll provision the peering override and watch RIBs. ETA 45m to apply.
Maya (CS): ETA works for them — demo at 10:30Z, they want changes in by 09:30Z to run verification. Please set a rollback alarm at +48h.
Tom (Infra): Applying change now in staging for canary. Config snippet I'll push (prod after canary pass): ```
customer_config:
  customer_id: "velveth-349"
  qps_limit: 800
  qps_previous: 200
  allowlist_cidrs:
    - "34.210.128.0/22"
    - "34.211.0.0/16"
    - "3.8.12.0/24"
  apply_window:
    start: "2024-11-08T08:00:00Z"
    end:   "2024-11-10T08:00:00Z"
  auto_rollback: true
``` 
Ravi (CS): Please also add a note to the renewal trackers — Velvet's execs said demo success impacts the renewal negotiation. Tagging as higher risk if we can't meet this.
Maya (CS): Will add to account health doc and send a short pre-demo checklist to the customer. Lina/Tom, ping me when both are done so I can confirm with Velvet.
Tom (Infra): Canary passed (09:02Z). Rolling to prod in 5. Will post varnish/cache invalidation commands after change.
Lina (NetOps): Peering override applied (09:07Z). BGP stable, no flaps observed.
Tom (Infra): Prod changes applied (09:12Z). Runbook command I used: ```
# invalidate small prefix cache
redwood cache invalidate --customer velveth-349 --prefix  /api/v1/partner
``` 
Maya (CS): I told the customer and they ran a quick smoke test — 95th p50 dropped from 420ms -> 120ms for UK testers. They are relieved. I'll update VT-4821 and the renewal note.
Ravi (CS): Great. Set to auto-revoke at 2024-11-10T08:00Z. If we see sustained load after that, we should propose a reserved capacity trial during renewal.
Lina (NetOps): Monitoring dashboards pinned to #cust-velvet for next 72h. Alerts set for CPU>75% and token latency > 350ms.
Maya (CS): Thanks all. Closing loop once auto-rollback fires. :thumbsup:
